chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from his men, who said:

He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah (Mighty and Majestic) has released for the executor the permission to change the bequest if it is not in accordance with what is customary/fair, and there is injustice in it, and to return it to what is customary/fair.
So whoever fears from the testator an inclination to a wrong course or an act of disobedience, and effects an agreement between the parties, then there is no blame on him.
Due to His (Mighty and Majestic) Words.

key_terms.بِالْمَعْرُوفِ: In accordance with what is customary/fair

ai.seo_question: What is the executor's right to modify a will if it is unjust?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the executor (al-wasi) holds the authority to rectify a bequest if it contains 'hayf' (injustice or deviation from equity), a principle grounded in the Quranic permission for 'islah' (reconciliation/adjustment). This ruling emphasizes the dynamic nature of wills, allowing the executor to correct errors or sins in the testator's distribution to ensure fairness among heirs, reflecting the broader Islamic legal concept of correcting unjust dispositions.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from his men who said,

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Released it for the executor that he can change the bequest when it does not happen to be with the goodness, and there was injustice in it, and return it to the goodness,

due to Hisazwj Words, the Mighty and Majestic [2:182] But he who fears an inclination to a wrong course or an act of disobedience on the part of the testator, and effects an agreement between the parties, there is no blame on him’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from his people who have said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has given permission to the executor of the will to change a will into an acceptable form if any violation of the law exists in it.
It is because of the meaning of the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious.
‘One who is afraid of the testator’s deviations and sin and settles the matter among the parties involved, he has not committed a sin. Allah is All-forgiving and All-merciful. 5 ” [2:182]
